name: Good Neighbors: The Axiom Block
description: One of the earliest and longest-running examples of the corponation lifestyle genre, Good Neighbors: The Axiom Block is a scripted drama-comedy hybrid following four families in an Axiom Consolidated residential block as they navigate everyday problems — minor debt restructuring, augmentation upgrade decisions, children's school placement — all of which are resolved through Axiom's resident services programs. The show has been running continuously since 2185 with cast rotations every seven years, and its theme music is recognizable to virtually every resident in GLMZ regardless of tier.
cultural_impact: The show's 40-year run has made its version of residential corponation life the cultural default — generations of Meridian residents use its fictional Axiom Block as their intuitive reference point for what 'normal' housing looks like.
story_hooks: A longtime cast member, beloved by Tier 1-2 audiences, has quietly been using their character's scripted scenes to embed coded messages to a Shelf mutual aid network for three seasons.
The original 2185 pilot contains a scene that was cut before broadcast — a scene that apparently depicts Axiom eviction procedures with uncomfortable accuracy.
A runner is hired to deliver a physical package to a retired writer from the show's first era, who claims the original premise was something very different before Axiom's creative team rewrote it.
